_comment: Two kinds, deliberately different — conflating them is how a gate becomes
expires    A TEMPORARY acceptance of a real, open risk. The check FAILS
once the date passes. Use whenever there is an open SEC ticket.
review_by  An accepted-BY-DESIGN exception, usually where an invariant's
heuristic is wrong rather than the risk being real. Emits a
notice once the date passes; never fails.
Every waiver needs ticket, owner and reason. A waiver that matches no live
finding is reported as stale and must be removed — waivers must not outlive

directly. Production carries ONLY the profile-photos finding; dev and
staging additionally carry search_by_contact_hash, which never shipped to

waivers.reason: Known open finding: the profile-photos bucket is world-readable, so avatars survive suspension and takedown. SEC-60 ('profile-photos storage bucket is fully world-readable') is still To Do. Tracked, not accepted — this waiver exists so the check can be switched on today without hiding the finding.

INV-4's body heuristic looks for is_admin / auth.uid() and finds neither. Verified by reading the live definition on 2026-07-27: this is a contact-hash lookup, not a privileged RPC. It is SECURITY DEFINER only so the hash comparison can bypass RLS, its search_path is pinned, and it returns rows only where is_published = true AND is_suspended = false (the SEC-80 fix). Any authenticated caller is meant to be able to call it. Never shipped to production.
As the dev entry above — same function, same verified definition. Staging mirrors dev for the phone/postcode discovery path that was never promoted to production.
